description: Cross-browser support: make BrowserSession engine-driven (chromium | firefox | webkit) from config (LAYA_BROWSER, default chromium), preserving Chromium channel support (chrome/msedge). Confine the engine selection to src/browser.ts. Install Firefox+WebKit for a real smoke test on at least one non-Chromium engine while keeping the default offline suite fast.
steps: In src/browser.ts import { chromium, firefox, webkit } from 'playwright' and add an `engine: 'chromium'|'firefox'|'webkit'` option to BrowserSessionOptions (default 'chromium'). In launch(), pick the browser type by engine; only pass `channel` for chromium (firefox/webkit have no channel). Keep everything else (viewport, timeouts, lazy launch, multi-tab, listeners) identical across engines.

In src/server.ts createServer, thread config.browserEngine into the BrowserSession options (browser: { engine: config.browserEngine, channel: config.channel, headless: config.headless, viewport: config.viewport }).
Install the non-Chromium engines needed for the smoke test: run `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && pnpm exec playwright install firefox webkit` (network is OPEN_INTERNET; they download).

Add test/cross-browser.test.ts that runs a SINGLE representative flow (navigate to login.html fixture, snapshot shows refs, type+click drives the form) on a non-Chromium engine — prefer firefox (usually the most reliable headless in Linux sandboxes); gate webkit behind an env flag or include it if it runs cleanly. Keep it to one or two smoke assertions so the default suite stays fast. If webkit cannot launch in the sandbox, gate that specific engine (describe.skipIf) and document why in findings; firefox must really run.
Confirm the default suite (chromium) is unaffected and still fast.
acceptance_criteria: BrowserSession launches chromium, firefox, or webkit driven by config.browserEngine, with channel applied only to chromium.
A cross-browser smoke test drives the login fixture to its literal signed-in outcome on at least one non-Chromium engine (firefox), really launching that engine (not skipped).
The default (chromium) suite remains green and fast.
Any engine that cannot run in the sandbox is gated with a documented reason, not faked.
typecheck + build + full test suite green.
findings: BrowserSession is now engine-driven. src/browser.ts imports { chromium, firefox, webkit }, adds engine:'chromium'|'firefox'|'webkit' to BrowserSessionOptions (default chromium) plus a BrowserEngineName export and a BROWSER_TYPES map; launch() uses the selected browserType and passes channel ONLY for chromium (firefox/webkit have no channel). Everything else (viewport, timeouts, lazy launch, multi-tab pages array, console/network/dialog listeners, routing, storage, resolveRef boundary) is unchanged and identical across engines. src/server.ts createServer now derives the browser session options from config (engine=config.browserEngine, headless, viewport, channel only when set), with an explicit options.browser override taking precedence and an injected session overriding both; src/index.ts stopped passing an explicit browser block and hands the config inward so LAYA_BROWSER flows through. Installed firefox+webkit via `pnpm exec playwright install firefox webkit` (network OPEN_INTERNET). test/cross-browser.test.ts runs a single representative sign-in flow (navigate login.html, snapshot shows [ref=eN], type email + click Sign in => status 'Signed in as cross@example.com', title 'Signed in', url #signed-in) parameterised by engine. firefox REALLY runs (not skipped): a module-load guard throws if the firefox binary is missing, and the test launched firefox in ~2.3s. WEBKIT GATED WITH DOCUMENTED REASON: the webkit binary downloads fine but launch() fails in this sandbox due to missing system shared libraries (Playwright host-requirements warning listed libs like libavif/libjpeg/libwoff2 etc). The test probes real launchability once at module setup (launch+close, not mere file existence) and uses describe.skipIf(!webkitLaunchable), so webkit is genuinely skipped here rather than faked; it will run automatically in an environment where WebKit can launch. Verification green: typecheck, build, and full suite (vitest run) all pass OFFLINE against local loopback fixtures = 119 passed | 3 skipped (was 118/2; +1 firefox test passing, +1 webkit test documented-skipped). Default chromium suite unaffected; total suite ~12.4s.
